correctness.rationale: Sum/difference transforms of disjoint independent microscopic payoffs give independent slopes of variance 4 and centered intercepts of variance m, independent across rows. Principal matrices are nonsingular almost surely; one affine system per open face bounds the count by 3^m. Requiring roots on all parallel edges maximizes the absolute offset to |h_i|+sum_{j≠i}|a_ij|/2 and forces the strict condition. Conversely dividing by the diagonals gives a strict self-map contraction on every free subcube. Fixed-coordinate normal rates have sign -sgn(a_ii); free-block Gershgorin discs remain strictly in their sign half-planes while off-diagonals shrink to zero, giving the asserted unstable dimension. A free unstable direction gives instability within its invariant face; a positive normal rate gives inward perturbations that grow, so the sink count is also valid relative to the full cube. Independence and sign symmetry then yield the q_m^m event and the 2^K count with K conditionally binomial. The three-ray spherical triangle for m=2 has angles pi/2, pi/4, pi/3, giving q_2=1/6. A separate exact cone integral and Jensen bound give log q_m=-(m/2)log m+(m/2)(1+log(2/pi))-log m+O(1), which in particular proves the stated remainder for the log joint probability. This does not depend on the finite checker or Monte Carlo figures.
residual_risks: Only the specified iid microscopic Gaussian law, local stability in the cube, and stationary-point counts are concluded; no basin sizes or Nash-only counts.

value.rationale: A joint probability of occupying every support face and a simultaneous local stability census answer different questions from marginal existence probabilities or expected counts. Their exact relation separates the many-stationary-state regime from the number of actual sinks; the sharp rarity asymptotic quantifies how rapidly this regime disappears as population number grows.
residual_risks: Mathematical benchmark, not an empirical prevalence or global dynamics claim.
